Orta nokta fomülü: In economics, the calculation method of dividing the net change by the average change in order to find the average percentage change.
Ortak değer ihalesi: The auction environment in which each participant assigns a value to the object of the auction depending on the others, and this value is decisive for everyone.
Ortak mal: Goods that are non-excludable in consumption but create rivalry.
Ortak malların trajedisi: The economics concept describing the destruction or damaging of the common resources shared by everyone in society as a result of personal interest and greed.
Ortalama değişken gider: Or in short AVC: the variable cost incurred per unit of product.
Ortalama gelir: Or in short AR: the revenue obtained per unit of product.
Ortalama harcama: Or in short AE: the expenditure made per unit of product.
Ortalama sabit gider: Or in short AFC: the fixed cost incurred per unit of product.
Ortalama toplam gider: Or in short ATC: the total cost incurred per unit of product.
Oto-Finansman: The practice of including, in the losses arising during resolution, not only the shareholders of the financial institutions but also those providing credit to these institutions.
Otomatik Dengeleyiciler: The fiscal elements that function spontaneously, quickly and effectively in the establishment and maintenance of economic balance. Progressive taxes and unemployment insurance payments can be given as examples.
Otomatik istikrarlandırıcı: The public budget elements that come into play spontaneously with the business cycles and have a reducing effect on the fluctuations in the economy.
Otonom değişken: In a mathematical model, the external effects that are not dependent on the other variables.
Otonom para talebi: The fixed portion of the demand for money that is not dependent on the interest rate, income or the general price level.
Otonom tüketim: The fixed portion of private consumption expenditures not dependent on income.
Otonom yatırım: The fixed portion of planned investments independent of income or the interest rate.
Oturum İzni: The other name of the residence permit that foreigners who have decided to settle in Türkiye for various reasons are obliged to obtain.
Oynaklık: The expression of the variability in an instrument's price. It is mostly measured with the standard deviation. High volatility is an indicator of increasing uncertainty.
Oyun kuramı: The body of principles explaining how economic units, acting in line with their own interest, will behave in mutual competition or cooperation.
Oyuncu: In game theory, the economic units whose behavior it is desired to explain.
Para: Any kind of object generally accepted as payment in return for goods and services.
Para arz eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between the nominal interest rate and the quantity of money in the economy, all else being constant.
Para arzı: Or in short MS: the quantity of money that the central bank, the commercial banks and the non-bank sector together bring into being in a given period.
Para benzeri: The securities that are close substitutes for money for transaction purposes.
Para Kurulu: An exchange rate regime permitting the printing of domestic currency in a country only up to the amount of foreign currency owned.
Para Piyasası: The market in which short-term (90 days or less for international markets), highly liquid financial instruments trade.
Para piyasası dengesi: The situation in which, in a given period, the quantity of money demanded in the market equals the quantity of money supplied.
Para piyasası fonu: Investment funds consisting of short-term, low-risk securities.
Para Politikası: Refers to the decisions taken with the aim of influencing the availability and cost of money in order to reach aims such as economic growth, increasing employment and price stability. The institutions responsible for its implementation are central banks. In the CBRT Law, it is stated that the fundamental aim of the CBRT is to ensure price stability.
Para Politikası Kurulu - PPK: The board formed within the CBRT, charged and authorized with determining the monetary policy principles and strategies with the aim of ensuring price stability, and, within the framework of these strategies, determining the inflation target together with the government, taking the measures necessary to preserve the internal and external value of the Turkish lira, and determining, again together with the government, the exchange rate regime directed at establishing its parity against foreign currencies and gold. The Monetary Policy Committee, under the chairmanship of the Governor, consists of the Deputy Governors, a member to be elected by the Bank Council from among its members, and a member to be appointed by joint decision upon the Governor's proposal. The Undersecretary of Treasury or the Deputy Undersecretary he designates may attend the meetings without voting rights.
Para talebi: Or in short MD: the quantity of money that all the units in the economy want to hold, depending on the interest rate, in a given period.
Para talep eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between the nominal interest rate and the quantity of money economic units want to hold, all else being constant.
Para taşıma ticareti: Or in short carry trade: the transaction of making gains by borrowing in a currency yielding low interest and investing in a currency yielding high interest.
Para ve Banka İstatistikleri: A stock data showing the money, deposits and other monetary liabilities of the central bank and the banks, the credits extended by these institutions, and their positions vis-à-vis abroad. By the residency principle, the transactions belonging to banks' foreign organizations are not included.
Para çarpanı: Or in short θ (read theta): the coefficient showing how much money will be created from one unit of reserves in the banking system.
Paranın Dolaşım Hızı: Shows how many units of goods or services one unit of money enables to change hands. It is expressed as GNP / Money Stock.
Paranın miktar kuramı: The body of principles maintaining that there is a same-directional and proportional relationship between the money supply and the general price level.
Paranın yansızlığı: The view maintaining that the money supply in the economy determines only the nominal magnitudes and will not affect the real values.
Parasal Aktarım Mekanizması: Shows through which channels and to what extent monetary variables affect aggregate demand, the output gap and inflation. The monetary transmission mechanism is generally explained in three stages. The first stage determines the transmission of the changes in monetary policy implementations to variables such as interest rates, asset prices, expectations and the exchange rate. In the second stage, the said variables affect the demand for domestic and imported goods; in the third stage, aggregate demand and domestic pricing behaviors are determined, and domestic prices and import prices shape inflation. In addition, interest rates have direct effects on inflation, and exchange rates on the demand for imported goods and on import prices in local currency.
Parasal Altın: Refers to the gold belonging to the central bank and held as reserves.
Parasal Büyüklükler: A monetary magnitude is calculated by subtracting the monetary sector's liabilities to one another from the total of the money in circulation and the various liabilities of the monetary sector (the central bank, banks and money market funds) that are monetary or convertible into money. There are various monetary magnitude definitions according to the degree of liquidity of the assets they contain: M1: consists of the total of the money in circulation and demand deposits. M2: consists of the total of M1 and time deposits. M3: M3, the most broadly defined money supply, consists of the total of M2, the funds provided from repos, money market funds and issued securities (with maturities of up to two years).
Parasal büyüme oranı kuralı: The monetary policy principle proposing that the central bank increase the money supply in proportion to the growth rate of real GDP.
Parasal gelir: The income consisting only of payments in the form of money.
Parasal hedefleme: The monetary policy regime in which the central bank targets a certain rate of increase for monetary magnitudes such as the money supply and bank reserves.
Parasal Sektör: It can also be defined as the money-creating sector. It covers the central bank, deposit banks, development and investment banks, participation banks and money market funds.
Parasalcı ekonomi kuramı: The school of thought maintaining that the changes seen in real income in the short run stem from demand shocks related to the money supply, and advocating the state's intervention in the economy through rule-based monetary policy.
Pareto etkinliği: The allocation of resources in which, while improving the situation of some individuals, no other individual's situation is worsened.
Parite: The value of one country's currency calculated against the currency of a reference country, with that country's currency taken as the basis.
Pasif iş arama: The state of waiting for responses to the applications previously made to the active job-search channels.
Patent Pool: Rival undertakings can assist R&D activities in the said area by opening the patents they hold to one another's use, with the aim of achieving a technological development. Undertakings coming together for a project gather the patents they hold in a pool and open them to the use of the other undertakings in the project.
